assessment: This study, one of the largest of its kind, replicates previous findings regarding the impairment of sleep rhythms in patients with schizophrenia relative to healthy controls. Specifically, sleep spindles, which constitute a hallmark of non-Rapid Eye Movement sleep, are less frequent in people with schizophrenia and several other sleep features were also affected. Overall, this study provides evidence that brain dynamics during sleep are promising biomarkers for the diagnosis and the prevention of schizophrenia.
